title: SDK labs playlist — daily scratch + tutorial fixes
summary: Day-to-day scratchpad for quick wins: small doc fixes, sample app checklist, clearing reproducible tutorial bugs, and low-effort examples to ship during sprint.
content:
Notes to self (quick wins and triage)

1) Micro-tasks to ship this week (priority order)
   - Fix streaming example in JS quickstart: current example omits headers for chunked responses; users hit timeout in browsers. Estimate: 1.5h. (issue: LINEAR-DEVX-1342)
   - Add minimal Python sync/async parity snippet for chat streaming in sdk-labs repo. Make both examples consistent with new 2026-02 runtime flags. Estimate: 2h.
   - Update SDK reference for "max_tokens" behavior with quantized models (note: runtime truncation changed in v0.9.1). Short paragraph + example. Estimate: 45m.

2) Repro steps I wrote down earlier (please keep)
   - Repro: tutorial "build-a-chat-widget" fails on step 4 when user clicks sample button. Error thrown: "unexpected token in stream".
     - Local repro: node 18.16, npm 10, running example with proxy to staging inference returns chunked HTTP but client expects JSON lines.
     - Quick fix: update fetch handler to handle streaming by parsing text chunks and JSON.parse on newline-delimited frames.

3) Quick code snippets to copy into docs (drafts)
   - Minimal node streaming snippet (pseudocode):
     const res = await fetch('/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', headers:{'Authorization': 'Bearer $KEY','Accept':'text/event-stream'}, body: JSON.stringify({model:'rw-infer-small', prompt:'hi'})});
     const reader = res.body.getReader();
     while(true){ const {value,done} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; processChunk(new TextDecoder().decode(value)); }

   - Python async example (aiohttp):
     async with session.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers) as resp:
       async for line in resp.content: handle_line(line.decode())

4) Doc gaps I keep seeing across labs and quickstarts
   - Missing guidance on when to pick dedicated vs hosted for dev/test workloads (we should add a small decision tree).
   - No clear example for "pinning model version" + rollout snippet (how to create canary route). Add a one-paragraph example + CLI commands.
   - Lack of a short page on "cost-aware defaults" for SDK: batching, cache TTLs, quantization tradeoffs. Users expect a single page summarizing knobs.

5) Sample app ideas (quick prototypes for workshops)
   - "Instant code mentor" — tiny webapp that calls Redwood chat APIs and displays token-level latency. Good demo for observability. Data: show per-request token cost and latency breakdown.
   - "Doc summarizer with pinned model" — demo: show how to pin a lightweight summarizer for cost control and fallback to larger model for long docs. Useful for Private customers.

6) Acceptance criteria for tutorial fixes (minimal):
   - Follow-the-steps works on Node 18 and latest Chrome with no extra flags.
   - Examples include both fetch (browser) and websocket/stream handler for server-sent events.
   - Tests: add a small integration smoke test that hits staging endpoint and asserts streaming payload decodes into at least one JSON chunk. Can stub network in CI.

7) Blockers & unknowns
   - Need confirmation from runtime team if streaming headers will change in next release (talk to @Ethan). If they change, we should gate examples behind a version note.
   - Does dedicated have a different base URL pattern we should document? I have a partial note but need official docs link.

8) Small PR checklist for docs edits
   - Update quickstart markdown + codeblock runtimes
   - Add captioned screenshot for console streaming viewer (capture from staging)
   - Link to rollout docs and to Dedicated URL docs
   - Run prettier / markdownlint on files before PR

9) Quick timeline for this sprint (what I will do)
   - Mon: streaming JS example fix + PR draft
   - Tue: python async example + tests, add to sdk-labs repo
   - Wed: write short decision tree + cost-aware defaults page stub
   - Thu: polish sample app README + smoke test
   - Fri: merge PRs, add follow-up tickets for bigger refactors

10) Random scratch notes (ideas, TODOs, reminders)
   - Consider adding small inline code sandbox embeds for JS examples so new users can click-run without keys (use a fake response or sandboxed proxy).
   - Add paragraph: "When to use streaming vs blocking generate" with 3 short bullets (latency-sensitive UI, long responses, token accounting).
   - Follow up with Solutions Eng to capture 2 customer examples where pinning saved >40% token cost.

-- end of scratchpad --

(If I lose this, pulling from linked_artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/842 or see LINEAR-DEVX-1342)
